<STRUCT_0001>
The goal of this section is to show that many algebraic stacks
<MATH_0001> have a ``stratification'' by locally closed substacks
<MATH_0002> such that each <MATH_0003> is
a gerbe. This shows that in some sense gerbes are the building blocks
out of which any algebraic stack is constructed. Note that by stratification
we only mean that
<MATH_0004>
is a stratification of the topological space associated to <MATH_0005>
and nothing more (in this section). Hence it is harmless to replace
<MATH_0006> by its reduction (see
Properties of Stacks, Section <REF_0001>)
in order to study this stratification.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
The following proposition tells us there is (almost always) a dense
open substack of the reduction of <MATH_0007>

Let <MATH_0001> be a reduced algebraic stack such that
<MATH_0002> is quasi-compact.
Then there exists a dense open substack <MATH_0003>
which is a gerbe.

According to
Proposition <REF_0001>
it is enough to find a dense open substack <MATH_0001> such that
<MATH_0002> is flat and locally of finite
presentation. Note that
<MATH_0003>, see
Lemma <REF_0002>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Choose a presentation <MATH_0004>. Let <MATH_0005> be the stabilizer
group algebraic space of the groupoid <MATH_0006>. By
Lemma <REF_0003>
we see that <MATH_0007> is the base change of
<MATH_0008> hence quasi-compact (by assumption)
and locally of finite type (by
Lemma <REF_0004>).
Let <MATH_0009> be the largest open (possibly empty) subscheme such that
the restriction <MATH_0010> is flat and locally of finite presentation
(we omit the proof that <MATH_0011> exists; hint: use that the properties are local).
By
Morphisms of Spaces, Proposition
<REF_0005>
we see that <MATH_0012> is dense. Note that <MATH_0013> is <MATH_0014>-invariant
by
More on Groupoids in Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0006>.
Hence <MATH_0015> corresponds to an open substack <MATH_0016> by
Properties of Stacks, Lemma
<REF_0007>.
Since <MATH_0017> is open and <MATH_0018> is dense we
conclude that <MATH_0019> is dense in <MATH_0020>.
Finally, the morphism <MATH_0021>
is flat and locally of finite presentation because the base change by
the surjective smooth morphism <MATH_0022> is the morphism
<MATH_0023> which is flat and locally of finite presentation by construction.
